metadata.title: ICILS 2023. Digitale Kompetenzen von Schülerinnen und Schülern im internationalen Vergleich
metadata.venue: Institut des Bundes für Qualitätssicherung im österreichischen Schulwesen (IQS)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICILS 2023 uses a two-stage stratified cluster sampling design: first, schools are selected via stratified random sampling; second, one or two classes are randomly selected within each participating school, and teachers are sampled within schools. The report states that analyses at the student level are conducted using the student weight from the corresponding dataset, while teacher-level analyses use the teacher weight; school leadership/IT-coordinator questionnaire data are weighted to the student population. It also notes that in Austria 7.6% of the national target population at the student level was excluded (with international reporting implications when exclusion rates exceed thresholds), indicating that weights account for differential selection and nonresponse/exclusion. The report does not provide the exact weight variable names in the extracted text, but it explicitly describes the weighting approach and applies it to produce population-representative estimates for comparisons across countries and benchmarks.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent outcomes in this report are scaled competence scores derived from Rasch modeling (reported as standardized scale scores and competence levels), not PV-based achievement indicators. Because the report does not describe a PV procedure and instead uses Rasch-based scaling, plausible values handling is not applicable in the PV sense; therefore PV-specific missing-data handling is not documented in the extracted sections. Missing data handling for questionnaire items is addressed only descriptively via missing-value thresholds in tables (e.g., marking items with high missingness), but the exact statistical missing-data method for the scaling/estimation is not specified in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target population: students in grade 8 (ICILS 2023) with an international age requirement (average around 13.5 years). Sampling is two-stage: stratified random selection of schools, then random selection of one or two classes per school; all students in selected classes are tested, and about 15 teachers per school are sampled. Exclusions at the student level in Austria are described as 7.6% weighted exclusion of the national target population, including exclusion of special schools, small schools, and minority-language schools, and exclusion codes for students with physical/mental impairments or insufficient German language proficiency. For reporting, the document also applies interpretive exclusions/flags: countries with high exclusion rates are marked and may not contribute to international benchmarks; small groups with weighted size <2.5% are not reported; and questionnaire items with high missingness are marked in annex tables (e.g., items with missingness thresholds m1–m4), with some items not reported when missingness exceeds 60%.

data.outcome_summary: ICILS 2023 is an IEA large-scale assessment of students’ digital competencies on grade 8, conducted in a five-year cycle (since 2013) and including an optional Computational Thinking domain since 2018. The report uses Rasch-based scaling to create competence scores and competence levels, standardizing the CIL scale (computer and information literacy) to a mean of 500 and SD of 100 internationally, and then reporting standardized national comparisons; competence levels are derived from score thresholds. Austria tested 3,448 students from 154 schools and applies complex survey weighting for student, teacher, and school-level questionnaire data. Results show Austria’s CIL mean of 506 points (above INT 476 and EU 493) and a Computational Thinking mean of 476 points (around INT/EU 483), with large shares of students at or below competence level 1 in both domains. The report emphasizes that the design is cross-sectional, so causal claims about national policies (e.g., the 8-point plan) cannot be made, and it flags limitations related to timing of policy implementation and COVID-19 disruptions.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a national results report for ICILS 2023 rather than an empirical machine-learning study. It provides descriptive and comparative statistics (means, standard deviations, competence-level distributions, and group differences) based on IEA scaling and survey-weighted estimation, but it does not train or evaluate ML models. Therefore, fields related to ML techniques and predictive findings are intentionally empty, and the extraction focuses on assessment design, sampling/weighting, and reported benchmarks.
